description:
## Finding
\`README.md:25\` crate-map row:
> \`pkix-revocation\` | CRL and OCSP revocation checking (offline) | core only | v0.2

A reader sees \`core only ✓\` and may interpret this as \"the entire crate is no_std with default features.\" That is not quite right. The real situation:

- The crate's *core* (\`NoRevocation\`, the \`RevocationChecker\` trait, \`Error\` enum) is no_std.
- The \`crl\` feature requires \`std\` (Cargo.toml:20: \`crl = [\"std\"]\`).
- The \`ocsp\` feature requires \`std\` and pulls in \`x509-ocsp\`, \`sha1\`, \`sha2\`.
- The \`std\` impl of \`std::error::Error\` is gated.

## Why P4
- \`pkix-revocation\` README explains this clearly (line 17–19).
- The workspace README compresses to \`core only ✓\` which is technically accurate but ambiguous.

## Fix
Change the workspace README crate-map cell to: \`core; CRL/OCSP need std\` or \`partial (NoRevocation only)\`.

## Scope reference
\`README.md:25\`.
title: P4: workspace README claim "core only ✓" for pkix-revocation no_std should clarify what "core only" means
